title: Sum of the solutions and unknown-coefficient roots
subtitle: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables  · 14 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **14 of the official questions in Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables  are this one** — 0 Easy, 2 Medium, 12 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You're asked for the sum of the solutions, a combination of roots from several equations, or a constant that makes the solutions add to a given value.
- Alternatively, the equation carries letters as coefficients and the choices are expressions, or you pick which of several expressions are solutions (I/II/III).

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Rewrite in standard form ax^2 + bx + c = 0.
- For a quadratic, the sum of the roots is -b/a, so you often don't need the roots themselves.
- 2) If a common factor appears on both sides, don't divide it away: move everything to one side and factor it out so that root isn't lost.
- 3) For higher degree, factor completely with the zero product property, list every root including ±√ roots, then add them or set the sum equal to the target.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: With numeric coefficients, graph it and add the x-intercepts.
With letter coefficients, turn them into sliders, check the choices against a trial value, and confirm the relationship holds as you move the sliders.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You divide both sides by a factor that contains x and lose a solution.
Or you use +b/a instead of -b/a, or forget to expand and combine terms before reading b and a.
On sums, you might also drop a root, since ±√k roots cancel in the sum but still count.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
